                                   MOTION TO DETERMINE NOTICE
                             REQUIREMENTS AND APPROVE FORM OF NOTICE

               COMES NOW Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company (“OG&E,” “Company,” or

        “Applicant”) and requests the Commission issue an order establishing notice requirements and

        approving form of notice in this Case. In support of this Motion, OG&E states as follows:

               1.      On June 17, 2026, OG&E filed its Application and Direct Testimony in this Case

        requesting that the Commission approve the Extra Large Power and Light Tariff, the Terms and

        Conditions of Service for Extra Large Load Customers, and a regulatory asset to track costs

        associated with the implementation of portfolio optimization software.

               2.      OAC 165:5-7-51(b) requires notice of hearing to be published once each week for

        two consecutive weeks at least fifteen days prior to hearing in a newspaper of general circulation

        published in each county in which affected utility customers are located, unless the Commission

        directs otherwise.

               3.      Newspapers of general circulation are not published in each county in which

        affected utility customers are located. Therefore, Applicant requests the Commission determine

        that for proposes of notice of hearing of the Application, notice be published in two newspapers of

        general circulation within the State of Oklahoma and also in newspapers of general circulation in




        OG&E Motion to Determine Notice Requirements                                           Page 1 of 6
 CASE PUD PUD2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 5 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 06/17/2026 - PAGE 2 OF 6




        the following Oklahoma counties: Alfalfa, Bryan, Dewey, Ellis, Grant, Jefferson, Johnston, Love,

        Major, Marshall, Woods, and Woodward.

               4.      Applicant proposes that the notice of hearing of the Application be published in

        The Oklahoman, Tulsa World, Medford Patriot Star, Cherokee Messenger & Republican, Alva

        Review-Courier, Enid News & Eagle, Woodward News, Northwest Oklahoman, Dewey County

        Record, The Ardmoreite, Johnston County Sentinel, Durant Democrat, Sequoyah County Times,

        Tahlequah Daily Press and The Poteau Daily News, once each week for two consecutive weeks

        at least fifteen days prior to the hearing on the merits. The proposed form of Notice of Hearing is

        attached to this Motion as Exhibit “A.”

               5.      Applicant represents that both the counties and publications as set forth in

        Paragraphs 3 and 4 are consistent with the Commission’s recent determinations for publication

        notice in OG&E matters as set forth in Order No. 743249 in Case No. PUD2024-000048 and Order

        No. 740764 in Case No. PUD 2023-000087.

               6.      The Commission has jurisdiction to grant the relief requested herein by virtue of

        Okla. Const. art. IX, § 18,17 O.S. § 152 et seq., and OAC 16:5-7-51(b).

               WHEREFORE, Applicant respectfully requests the Commission issue an order

        determining notice requirements of one a week for two consecutive weeks at least 15 days prior to

        the hearing in the above-identified publications and approving the form of notice substantially in

        the form of Exhibit “A” as requested herein.

                                             NOTICE OF HEARING
                 NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company (“OG&E”)
        filed its Application requesting approval of an Extra Large Power and Light Tariff, the Terms and
        Conditions of Service for Extra Large Load Customers with expected energy demand of 75
        megawatts or more, and a regulatory asset to track costs associated with the implementation of
        portfolio optimization software.
               NOTICE IS FUTHER GIVEN the Tariff is designed to provide specific rates and terms
        and conditions of service to ensure the addition of Extra Large Load Customers does not adversely
        impact other customer classes, and in fact, creates benefits for residential customers.
               NOTICE IS FURTHER GIVEN that a Hearing on the Merits is set before an
        Administrative Law Judge on the ____ day of ___________ at _____ _.m. and continuing until
        the record is closed at the Oklahoma Corporation Commission in the Concourse Theater, Suite
        C50, Will Rogers Office Building in the Capitol Complex, 2401 N. Lincoln Boulevard, Oklahoma
        City, Oklahoma 73105. The Concourse Theater is located in the tunnel between the Will Rogers
        Office Building and the Sequoyah Office Building.
               NOTICE IS FURTHER GIVEN that all interested persons may appear and be heard
        regarding issues in this Case, and the Commission shall, after hearing, issue such orders and grant
        such relief as it deems fair, just, reasonable, and in the public interest, whether or not specifically
        requested in the Application.
               For further information regarding the application, contact A. Chase Snodgrass, Deborah R.
        Thompson, or Kenneth A. Tillotson, Attorneys for Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company, P.O. Box
        54632, Oklahoma City, OK 73154, telephone (405) 955-2285; or ________, Counsel for the
        Oklahoma Corporation Commission Public Utility Division, Will Rogers Building, 2401 N.
        Lincoln Blvd., Oklahoma City, OK 73105, phone (405) 522-8088; or Thomas L. Grossnicklaus,
        Deputy Attorney General, Office of the Attorney General, 313 NE 21st Street, Oklahoma City, OK
        73105, telephone (405) 521-3921 or by email at utility.regulation@oag.ok.gov.
